name: energy
title: Energy balance and costs
description: Read this workspace's Energy: what is left, what each action costs, this month's use and renewal, or with estimate what planned work will cost against the balance. Use it to check coverage before large discovery or X work, paid profile or email lookups, or standalone recent-X-post reads (lookups add to discovery; cached lookups are free). Discovery, lookups and X outreach use Energy; LinkedIn and email sending use none. Checking prices does not require narrating the balance: show it only when asked or it blocks the work. Execute requested work within existing Energy and agreed usage without another confirmation; before exceeding agreed usage, show a concise estimate and ask. Reading is free and works at zero. When Energy runs short, say what the work needs and what is left, and offer the smallest top-up from the response's refill guidance (a pack is $10 for 75 Energy, or 100 per $10 from $50 up); mention a bigger plan only when the customer asks or refill.plan says to. Team members ask the billing owner, and an allocation limit needs an allocation change. Read-only: buys nothing and changes no setting. Returns the balance (remaining, total, costs, usage, renewal, automatic top-up state, refill guidance and the links that open) or, with estimate, the planned work's cost and whether the balance covers it.

Lists are bounded previews with totals and hasMore, not the whole inventory. Respect metric units and periods, and never assign action totals to a channel by guessing. Missing optional channels, LinkedIn included, do not block other channels. Follow scoped attention and returned Accounts/Billing/Company links, and never invent an onboarding requirement. When attention includes leads_waiting_for_input, say who is waiting and for what before anything else (list_leads waitingForInput=true lists them); sender_file_reconnect_required means that X account must be reconnected on Accounts before its files can send; its other messages keep sending. name: reach_post_engagers

LinkedIn post URL plus message: PumpGTM creates a Play with its own approved sequence (note-less connection request, then your message and any followUps), fetches every reactor and commenter in the background (up to 500), and enrolls all of them; call again with only playId for progress. Report polling blockers and paused Sequences exactly as returned; do not promise polling or sending while blocked. Follower Plays can still receive incoming X follow events while fallback polling is blocked. Read the returned X Play with list_x_plays, change its audience or sequence with edit_x_play, and turn on automatic enrollment with set_x_play_status only when the customer requests it. watchId alone checks source/Sequence progress. name: add_leads
title: Add leads to a sequence
description: Add people the customer already has (exact LinkedIn URLs, a CSV, a saved Sales Navigator list or supplied contacts) to one approved sequence: contacts accepts 1–500 supplied people with LinkedIn, email, and/or X identities plus expectedRevision. It supports X-only and email-only contacts, preserves supplied fields, performs no paid enrichment, skips existing identities across all channels, and keeps paused sequences paused. Other methods accept manual LinkedIn profiles, CSV content, or a saved Sales Navigator list URL. LinkedIn profile links accept literal or percent-encoded accents and emoji, with HTTPS or a bare linkedin.com/in/... link. name: set_lead_input
title: Store a per-person value or file for a held message
description: Store a value or file the customer supplies for one person, such as a link to a video they recorded, so a LinkedIn message, email, X DM or Instagram DM step declared with tool customer_input can send. Identify the person by exactly one of leadId, linkedinUrl, email or xUsername. values maps the sequence's token names (for example video_url) to the customer's text; the key comes from the sequence, the customer never types it. One call fills every step of that person's sequence that uses the token and has not sent yet. A link to a video (Loom, YouTube, Drive) is a text value such as video_url, not a file. A step declared with an attachment takes a file per person instead: call with upload to get a one-time uploadUrl, PUT the bytes there with the returned headers, then call again with files; if you cannot upload bytes yourself, give the customer the returned appUrl to add the file in the app. For several people at once use uploads, then confirmUploads; the customer has already decided which file is whose, so do not second-guess their pairing. Nothing is compressed: a larger file is refused with the limit and the way forward, which you relay as written. Nothing is sent in this call: the paced engine sends on its next run if the person is at that step, or when they reach it. A value or file for someone who already replied, finished, or already received that message is refused with nothing changed. Returns what was stored for each person and how many people in that sequence are still waiting; afterwards list_leads with sequenceId and personalFiles=true shows which file each person has. Open world: the stored value releases a held message to that person, a third party.

name: save_sequence_draft
title: Create or edit a sequence draft
description: Write or edit an outreach sequence (LinkedIn, email and X messages) as a draft that sends nothing. Without sequenceId: create a complete new sequence (name plus ordered steps). With sequenceId and expectedRevision: read the full draft first, then replace its complete step list using that exact revision, preserving next, condition, sendIf and other unchanged fields; an active or paused sequence must be reopened with set_sequence_status status=draft first. The result is always an unapproved draft: show the customer the copy and its reviewUrl, and only after they approve this exact revision call set_sequence_status status=approved with expectedRevision, which makes it live; do that before adding people. Before writing copy, follow the writing, follow-up and connection-note rules on the steps field; never invent a customer, number or link. Steps include connect, message, engage (LinkedIn), email (subject plus body), x_dm and x_engage; executionModel sets the step limits and routing, and each step field explains placeholders, per-person values and files. Graph outreach first checks earlier email, LinkedIn and X conversations: a human reply stops it and unavailable evidence holds it. On reconnectXForFiles, tell the customer to reconnect that X account on Accounts before files can send; other messages keep sending. Returns the saved sequence (creation or update), its reviewUrl, nextStep and the approval call to make next.

steps.description: The complete ordered step list, a replacement rather than a patch. Read the full sequence before editing and retain unchanged routing and sendIf fields. Write like a person typing a DM to a colleague: concrete point first, plain words, contractions and natural rhythm. No em dashes, preambles ('Here's the thing'), formal transitions, mirrored contrasts ('not X, but Y'), rhetorical-question chains, slogans, buzzwords, tidy groups of three, or forced hooks, punchlines and takeaways; ask at most one question. Read it aloud and keep only what the sender would really say. Every new sequence and LinkedIn post-engagers Play gets three follow-ups after the first message unless the customer wants fewer: proof (+2 days: a company like the prospect's, one result with a number, one link), a question about how they do that job today or an offer of something free (+3 days), and a short last note that leaves the door open (+5 days), all in the customer's voice from their first message and company. Never invent a customer, number or link: ask for a real result before saving, and use the free offer in place of proof when they have none. LinkedIn connection requests go without a note: never suggest, offer or draft one, because it makes the request read overly specific. Only if the customer insists, put it in the connect step's messageTmpl (at most 300 characters; only {{firstName}} {{fullName}} {{company}} {{title}} {{senderFirstName}}); an account out of notes sends the request without it. Instagram DMs run only in their own linear sequence. Linear sequences that use LinkedIn start with connect, and linear X sequences cannot mix channels. After any lead leaves graph step 0, only copy and delay edits are accepted.

executionModel.description: linear: up to 20 ordered steps; delayDays counts from the previous step and the step after connect waits for acceptance. tracks: up to 20 steps in parallel LinkedIn, email and X lanes; delays count from each lane's previous step and a missing channel does not block other lanes. graph: up to 30 nodes with explicit next targets, branch conditions and one cursor; action delays start when that node is reached, waiting branches use delayDays as their window. connect may sit anywhere, once per path; a LinkedIn message or endorsement must come after a connection request and an 'Accepted?' (linkedin_accepted) or 'Already connected?' (linkedin_first_degree) Yes path; view, like and comment need no connection; missing email or X identity skips that channel's action. Defaults to linear on create; omission on edit preserves the saved model. Changing models requires no existing execution progress.

name: decide_reply
title: Apply the customer's reply decision
description: Apply one explicit human decision to a pending reply. send, invite, and booking_link contact the prospect at once; opt_out is permanent. Show the draft and ask the customer first.
